chose: The sample week behind the rows tells one story so each row's colours decide something. Each night a render job is named to the lane at 23:15 and admitted, and the lane's decisions are paulgsc/server's own (crates/lane `step`, ported tick by tick with file_host's policy: 2 GiB floor, 10 % pressure limit, 30 s hold-down): it pauses the render while interactive work waits (23:25 to 23:35), stops it once when memory pressure passes its limit (23:40, one stop), settles, and runs it again. The window ends at 00:00 with the render on the cores, so the rows' instant stats show it live: latency past its orange line, load shed (REFUSALS red), the transcriber's oldest note past its promise (SLOW), one stop of this job (orange). Besides: two deploys (RESTARTS 2), NATS down twenty minutes, a scraper meeting the limiter, an hour of ESPN timeouts, twenty minutes of the mailbox not answering (NOT OK orange), a nightly backup as iowait. Every outcome happens at least a little, since a bar of no length is drawn unevenly. The stage draws every pixel on the CPU (Chromium's GPU raster paths off), since a canvas chart's antialiasing otherwise differed by a pixel between loads; with it, fresh runs give identical screens.
options: a week whose stats are all green at its end (C1433, moved)
a week that ends inside the nightly render, so the rows show a live decision (chosen)
a different incident at the end, such as an outage
